Required findings: Pre‑ and post‑test genetic counseling performed by an appropriate provider as defined by the health plan
No prior full BRCA1/2 sequencing or deletion/duplication analysis performed; if any prior BRCA testing was done, it did not identify a pathogenic variant and does not explain the current indication

Meets at least one Diagnostic Testing for Symptomatic Individuals criterion: • Ashkenazi Jewish descent with epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, primary peritoneal, breast (any age), exocrine pancreatic, or prostate cancer (any age) • Female breast cancer diagnosed ≤50 years • Two or more primary breast cancers of any age • Triple‑negative breast cancer (ER‑, PR‑, HER2‑) of any age • Male breast cancer of any age • Epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer of any age • Prostate cancer of any age with metastatic disease, intraductal/cribriform histology, high‑risk or very‑high‑risk per NCCN • Exocrine pancreatic cancer of any age • Personal & Family History Combination (initial breast cancer at any age plus a first‑/second‑/third‑degree relative with breast cancer ≤50 y, ovarian/fallopian tube/peritoneal cancer any age, or a close relative with triple‑negative breast cancer, metastatic prostate cancer, pancreatic cancer, or two close relatives with breast/prostate cancer)

Non-Indications: Any prior full BRCA1/2 sequencing or deletion/duplication analysis already performed
Previous genetic testing that would have detected the familial mutation (e.g., known familial mutation already tested)
Absence of required genetic counseling documentation
No qualifying personal or family cancer history as defined in the diagnostic criteria
Ashkenazi Jewish founder testing attempted without meeting the specific ancestry or cancer‑history requirements
Testing performed when a more informative affected relative is available and can be tested instead of the unaffected member
Important criteria & exceptions: Rendering laboratory must be a qualified provider per health‑plan policy
For Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutation testing, patient must have no prior full sequencing, deletion/duplication, or founder testing and must meet either symptomatic or presymptomatic criteria
If the most informative affected relative cannot be tested, the ordering physician must document why the unaffected member is being tested
Deletion/duplication analysis component (required for CPT 81162) is only reimbursable when the patient also meets full‑sequence criteria and has no prior deletion/duplication test
Documentation required: Pre‑test genetic counseling note signed by qualified provider
Prior genetic testing reports (if any) confirming no previous full sequencing or deletion/duplication

Pathology or operative reports confirming cancer diagnoses that satisfy diagnostic criteria (e.g., breast cancer ≤50 y, triple‑negative status, ovarian/fallopian tube/peritoneal cancer, prostate cancer with metastatic/high‑risk features, exocrine pancreatic cancer)
Detailed family history pedigree documenting degree of relationship, cancer types, ages at diagnosis, and Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry when applicable
Laboratory requisition indicating CPT 81162 and confirming that the rendering laboratory is qualified
